Prepare LE8 inputs for multiple imputation with mice

Source: R/imputation.R
le8_imputation_setup.Rd

le8_imputation_setup() returns the settings mice::mice() needs to multiply impute missing score_le8() inputs in a way the AHA scoring rules can use. score_le8(impute = TRUE) uses them to impute and score in one call; call le8_imputation_setup() yourself to inspect the settings, or to adjust them and run mice directly, then score the result with score_le8_imputed().

Imputing the inputs, rather than the 0-100 scores, keeps the relationships between measurements that the AHA bands then summarize. The setup encodes what is specific to LE8:

  • Only inputs a person's age uses are imputed. For example, adult BMI is never imputed for a child, nor blood-pressure percentile thresholds for an adult, nor a MEPA item that a preschooler's screener does not include. Observed values in such structurally unused cells are set to NA in the prepared data so they cannot distort the imputation models. years_since_quit is imputed only for adults who are, or may be imputed as, former smokers.

  • Predictors are limited to inputs available (observed or imputed) for everyone the target applies to, plus age and any auxiliary columns, so no model relies on structurally missing values.

  • Methods: predictive mean matching ("pmm") for numeric inputs, which imputes only observed values and so respects their range and skew; logistic regression ("logreg") for two-level inputs; and multinomial regression ("polyreg") otherwise. Logical and character inputs are converted to factors for mice; score_le8_imputed() converts them back.

  • Combinations AHA does not score are never imputed. Diagnosed diabetes implies an HbA1c measure. Current combustible smoking is never paired with current inhaled-NDS use. An observed fasting glucose implies no diagnosed diabetes, and an observed HbA1c of 6.5% or more implies diagnosed diabetes. Each imputed glucose value comes from donors with the same measure and diabetes status, and a measure is imputed only if such donors exist. These rules run in mice's post step of every iteration, so the other imputation models condition on consistent values.

Two values that follow from observed data are filled in before imputation (deductive imputation): glucose_measure is "hba1c" when diabetes is TRUE, and current_inhaled_nds is FALSE for current smokers.

Usage

le8_imputation_setup(data, auxiliary = NULL, diet_method = "mepa")

Arguments

data

A data frame of score_le8() inputs.

auxiliary

Optional character vector of other columns in data to use as predictors, such as analysis outcomes, exposures, or survey design variables. They must be complete; they are not imputed.

diet_method

The diet scoring method; only "mepa" is supported.

Value

An essential8_imputation_setup object, a list with the prepared data and the mice arguments method, predictorMatrix, where, visitSequence, and post, plus inputs, a data frame describing each input: the rows it applies to, the values to impute, and the method.

Details

Observed values are validated with score_le8() first, so data that cannot be scored stop here rather than after imputation. Every observed glucose_value needs its glucose_measure.

Only the MEPA diet screener is supported. Inputs must use the default column names, and age must be complete.

With adults and children in one data set, inputs that apply to only one population cannot predict inputs that apply to both. To use richer models, impute each population separately and combine the results with rbind(), which mice provides for mids objects.

Imputation models should include the variables used in later analyses, such as exposures and outcomes. Pass them in auxiliary.

score_le8(impute = TRUE) calls mice::mice() with remove.collinear = FALSE and remove.constant = FALSE. mice's defaults would stop imputing an input that is constant or collinear in the observed data, leaving values that scoring needs missing. Each imputation model still drops such predictors on its own. When calling mice::mice() directly with a setup, pass the same two arguments.

Glucose values mix units (mg/dL for fasting glucose, % for HbA1c), so glucose_measure and glucose_value predict only each other; diabetes represents glucose status in the other models.

See also

score_le8() and its impute argument to impute and score in one call; le8_imputation_control(); score_le8_imputed() to score your own mice run.

Examples

adults <- read.csv(system.file(
  "extdata", "le8-adult-example.csv", package = "essential8"
))
adults <- adults[!startsWith(names(adults), "expected_")]
adults$non_hdl_cholesterol[c(2, 5)] <- NA
adults$sleep_hours[3] <- NA

setup <- le8_imputation_setup(adults)
setup
#> LE8 imputation setup: 10 rows; 3 missing input values to impute in 2 inputs
#> 
#>                input applies_to missing impute method
#>          sleep_hours         10       1      1    pmm
#>  non_hdl_cholesterol         10       2      2    pmm

# Adjust the settings, then run mice yourself: here, sleep hours are no
# longer predicted from age. Keep predictive mean matching for numeric
# inputs; methods such as "norm" can impute values outside their valid
# range, which score_le8() then rejects.
setup$predictorMatrix["sleep_hours", "age"] <- 0
imputed <- mice::mice(
  setup$data,
  m = 5,
  method = setup$method,
  predictorMatrix = setup$predictorMatrix,
  where = setup$where,
  visitSequence = setup$visitSequence,
  post = setup$post,
  remove.collinear = FALSE,
  remove.constant = FALSE,
  seed = 1,
  printFlag = FALSE
)
#> Warning: Number of logged events: 110
summary(score_le8_imputed(imputed))
#> LE8 scores: 10 participants (10 adult), pooled over 5 imputations
#> Diet method: mepa; min_components: 7
#> Composite score available for 10 of 10 (average over imputations).
#> 
#>                    n mean    95% CI  fmi   sd median
#> LE8 composite     10 48.6 27.1-70.1 0.19 29.1   50.9
#> Diet              10 51.0 22.9-79.1 0.19 38.1   50.0
#> Physical activity 10 60.0 35.2-84.8 0.19 33.7   70.0
#> Nicotine exposure 10 40.0 15.4-64.6 0.19 33.3   30.0
#> Sleep             10 58.0 31.0-85.0 0.26 34.8   64.0
#> BMI               10 46.5 20.2-72.8 0.19 35.7   50.0
#> Blood lipids      10 45.2 17.5-72.9 0.23 36.3   40.0
#> Blood glucose     10 46.0 22.6-69.4 0.19 31.7   50.0
#> Blood pressure    10 42.0 19.4-64.6 0.19 30.7   40.0
#> Means pooled with Rubin's rules; fmi = fraction of missing information.
#> 
#> Category (rows with a composite score):
#>            n percent    95% CI
